speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you mentioned a generalized nonpruritic rash and a history of high fever and seizure; has this rash appeared suddenly or gradually, and do you have any known drug allergies or recent travel history?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola infantum (Exanthem Subitum) caused by Human Herpesvirus 6 (HHV-6).

I am confident this diagnosis is correct given the classic presentation of high fever followed by a rash once the fever subsides, along with a febrile seizure in an infant with up-to-date immunizations. No further tests are required at this time.
